correctness.rationale: Theorem 4.7 of Garity–Repovš (2013) supplies the fundamental-group isomorphism for a wedge with a simply connected second complement. Theorem 5.4 supplies unchanged local genus off the wedge point and the sum formula at it, so the bound is \(B+1\). The derived-set proof is explicit: finite inherited genus-one points are isolated in \(L_1(Y)\), while the genus-one factor is perfect and hence its non-wedge points are non-isolated; the wedge point is handled separately according as \(g_x(C)=0\) or at least \(1\).

evidence: Garity–Repovš (2013), Question 8.1: asks whether examples with the same complement fundamental group can have all local genera bounded; the paper says its own wedge constructions can have arbitrarily large genus.
Garity–Repovš–Wright (2014), Theorem 4.2 and Theorem 4.4: gives an uncountable family of rigid genus-one examples with simply connected complements.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The 2013 theorem already gives many same-group examples, but its genus-marker construction is not bounded. The present theorem changes the construction: it uses a genus-one factor and the derived set of L1(Y) to distinguish it, giving a uniform B+1 bound when the base has finite L1. This is a conditional extension, not a solution for all bases.
